title: Learning that sticks
text: {{1}} is tempting to cram: the exam looms, the book is open, the coffee is cold. {{2}} the long run, however, the crammer remembers almost nothing, because memory is built {{3}} forgetting a little and then being reminded at the right moment. {{4}} a fact is recalled just as it begins to fade, the effort of retrieval makes the memory {{5}} durable, and {{6}} the next review can wait a little longer {{7}} the last. {{8}} is the effect that ten minutes a day with a flashcard app can hold vocabulary in place for years, while a week of cramming evaporates before the certificate is dry.

gaps.hint: dummy subject: ___ is tempting to cram
gaps.explanation: 'It is tempting to…' — the dummy subject before the infinitive.
'In the long run' is the fixed phrase.

gaps.hint: preposition: built ___ forgetting and being reminded
gaps.explanation: 'By + gerund' — the means of building memory.

gaps.hint: conjunction: ___ a fact is recalled just as it fades
gaps.explanation: Time clause governing the strengthening: when.
The comparative 'more durable' — first element gapped.

gaps.hint: adverb: and ___ the next review can wait
gaps.explanation: 'And so' — the consequence within the added clause.

gaps.hint: comparative: a little longer ___ the last

gaps.explanation: Fronted inversion: 'Such is the effect that…'.
